name: tornado
why: Reference Python async web framework; small enough to scan in seconds yet carries real cross-module duplication: sibling data-structure tests restated from one another, a hand-stamped demo suite, and copy-pasted raw-HTTP test scaffolding.

ceilings.rationale: 1024 MB, sized to this corpus: 110 analysed files, about a fifth of tokio, measured at roughly 2 s wall on a development machine. The wall ceiling is deliberately loose - it exists to catch a hang, not to police throughput.

must_find.why: The fetch_json test helper is defined twice, byte for byte: fetch, rethrow, and json_decode the response body. Same statements, same order, same names, in two test modules.
must_find.verified: diff of tornado/test/httpserver_test.py:83-86 against tornado/test/web_test.py:894-897 at the pinned sha is empty - zero differing bytes.

must_find_status: CURATED. One cross-file exact-copy family, verified by an empty diff at the pinned sha. Hand verification also found byte-identical duplication confined to single files (the Subprocess.initialize preamble triplet in tornado/test/process_test.py:192-194 and 202-204, and a two-line assertion couplet repeated seven times in tornado/test/tcpclient_test.py), which the cross-file `files` list cannot express; recorded as prose ground truth for a future same-file assertion form.

must_find_type2.why: test_get_clears_timed_out_putters in queues_test.py is the locks_test test_garbage_collection restated against the sibling Queue data structure: same comprehension of timed-out operations with timedelta(seconds=0.01), same one-more-operation watermark check on len(._waiters/_putters), the same yield gen.sleep(0.02) collection window, the same 'Final waiter is still active.' comment carried over verbatim, and the same trailing assertRaises(TimeoutError) drain loop. The queue version adds a get-clears-waiters pair of statements.
must_find_type2.verified: Read both regions in full at the pinned sha. Statement-for-statement the same order with the data structure and identifiers renamed (Semaphore/acquire/_waiters vs Queue/put/_putters) plus the extra q.put(11)/q.get() pair that is the queue test's actual subject; the shared comments are byte-identical, which no independent authorship produces.

must_find_type2.why: The raw-HTTP response stub in routing_test.py request_callable is the httpserver_test.py header-length probe stamped into a second file: the same write_headers(ResponseStartLine("HTTP/1.1", 200, "OK"), HTTPHeaders({"Content-Length": ...})) followed by connection.write(b"...") and connection.finish(), differing only in the content-length literal source and the body bytes.
must_find_type2.verified: Read both regions in full at the pinned sha. The five-statement sequence is identical in order; the only differences are the receiver name (self.connection vs request.connection), the Content-Length value expression, and the body literal b"1234567890" vs b"OK".

must_find_type2.why: The body-expected/body-present validation in the two HTTP clients is the same block duplicated across production modules: the identical double-condition guard, the identical ValueError message text, and the identical conditional 'not ' prefix, differing only in indentation depth and request.method vs self.request.method.
must_find_type2.verified: diff of tornado/curl_httpclient.py:446-453 against tornado/simple_httpclient.py:412-419 at the pinned sha shows only leading whitespace and the receiver expression; every other character, including the full multi-part message string, is identical.

must_find_type2.why: The demos are one application stamped out three times. blog.py and chatdemo.py build the same tornado.web.Application with a hand-written route list, the identical placeholder cookie_secret="__TODO:_GENERATE_YOUR_OWN_RANDOM_VALUE_HERE__", template_path and static_path resolved from os.path.dirname(__file__), xsrf_cookies=True and a debug flag.
must_find_type2.verified: Read both regions in full at the pinned sha. The settings payload is the same key sequence with only the route table entries, the blog_title key, and debug=True vs debug=options.debug differing.

must_find_type2.why: The logout handler is copy-pasted between the facebook and google_auth demos: a RequestHandler subclass whose get() clears a demo cookie and redirects to /.
must_find_type2.verified: Read both regions in full at the pinned sha. The class body is statement-for-statement identical; only the class name, the mixin in the base list, and the cookie name literal differ.

must_find_type2_status: CURATED. Six cross-file pairs hand-verified by reading both regions in full at the pinned sha and stating exactly what differs; the min_nodes floors sit well below the canonical node counts the pinned-sha scan rendered to leave build-to-build drift headroom. Thirty further pairs were hand-verified during the same two-pass curation pass and are recorded here as prose ground truth: the strongest are same-file pairs the cross-file files list cannot express - the max_wbits validation duplicated inside tornado/websocket.py (739-748 vs 789-797, near-identical), the byte-identical Subprocess preamble triplet in tornado/test/process_test.py (192-194 vs 202-204), the f/future semaphore-acquire rename pair in tornado/test/locks_test.py (290-293 vs 440-443), the days=10/days=2 cookie-expiry pair in tornado/test/web_test.py (486-491 vs 3176-3181), and the wait/acquire condition rename pair in tornado/test/locks_test.py (53-55 vs 254-256). The same pass confirmed precision verdicts: an older engine build reported tornado/test/auth_test.py:501-505 together with tornado/test/web_test.py:2314-2318 (OAuth login tests against HTTP handler method definitions - shape-only, unrelated code, its own embedding signal scored 0.0) and that pairing is absent from the current report; the current report also correctly suppresses seven-times-repeated two-line tcpclient_test.py assertion boilerplate that the older build published. Those verdicts are recorded so the next curation pass re-checks them rather than re-derives them.
